issues.legal_issue: A statutory development scheme may be altered only through the designated authority’s reasoned, formal decision that the alteration improves the scheme for the public.
material_facts: The sanctioned scheme reserved the disputed open space for a public park.
The authority’s chairman sought conversion of the park site after the private trust requested it for a hospital, and the government directed and approved the conversion and allotment.
The authority adopted a resolution implementing the government’s decision, but no formal consideration by the authority of whether the alteration would improve the scheme was shown.
The court found that the process was directed toward benefiting a particular private trust rather than establishing a public improvement.
issues.conclusion: The scheme was not validly altered; the conversion and allotment were invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 19(4) of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976, the authority may alter a scheme only if it appears to the authority that the alteration would improve some part of the scheme. The decision must be made objectively and rationally by the authority in the manner appropriate to a body corporate, and must serve the scheme’s public purpose rather than confer a private benefit. Sections 19(5) and 19(6) prescribe circumstances in which government sanction is relevant. The Court relied on the principle stated in Shri Sitaram Sugar Company Limited v. Union of India that statutory discretion must be exercised within the statute’s limits.

rule.if: writ_challenge_to_development_scheme_action and scheme_change_for_private_benefit and (not authority_formally_decided_change or not objective_public_improvement_assessment)

predicates.writ_challenge_to_development_scheme_act: A person or group brought a writ challenge to action changing a statutory development scheme.
predicates.scheme_change_for_private_benefit: The proposed change to the scheme was directed toward conferring a benefit on a particular private party.
predicates.authority_formally_decided_change: The designated statutory authority formally considered and decided to make the scheme change.
predicates.objective_public_improvement_assessment: The authority objectively assessed whether the change would improve the scheme for the public.

issues.definition: When a private-benefit scheme change is challenged and the designated authority did not formally decide on it or objectively assess its public improvement, the scheme alteration is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: A government direction to a statutory development authority cannot require action contrary to the governing statute or the purpose of the development scheme.
material_facts: The government ordered the conversion of an area reserved for a public park and approved its allotment to a private trust.
The authority implemented those directions rather than independently deciding whether the statutory conditions for changing the scheme were met.
The proposed action conflicted with the statutory purpose of orderly development and preservation of public open space.
issues.conclusion: The government’s directions were beyond the permissible scope of its powers, and the resulting action was invalid.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 15(3) and 65 of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976 do not confer unrestricted power on the government to direct the authority. Directions must be reasonably necessary or expedient to carry out the Act’s purposes and cannot displace the specific power and conditions in Section 19(4). General powers cannot validate action that the statute does not permit. The authority must exercise its own statutory responsibilities rather than abdicate them to the government.

predicates.writ_challenge_to_statutory_authority_ac: A person or group brought a writ challenge to action taken by a statutory authority following a government direction.
predicates.government_directed_action_contrary_to_s: The government directed action inconsistent with the purpose of the governing statute or scheme.
predicates.authority_implemented_direction_without_: The statutory authority implemented the direction without independently making the decision entrusted to it by law.

issues.definition: When a challenged government direction conflicts with the statute’s purpose and the authority implements it without independent decision, the direction and resulting action are invalid.

issues.legal_issue: Land reserved for a public park cannot be diverted to a different use or allotted to a private party merely because the proposed use may provide a public or civic service.
material_facts: The sanctioned scheme reserved the only available open space in the area for a public park.
The government converted the site into a civic-amenity site and the authority allotted it to a private trust for a hospital.
The proposed hospital was privately owned and managed, while the park was reserved for public recreation, ventilation, and environmental protection.
issues.conclusion: The park site could not lawfully be diverted and allotted for the private hospital; the orders and allotment were null and void.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 16(1)(d) and 16(2)(b) of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976 distinguish public parks and playgrounds from civic amenities and recognize open space for ventilation. Section 30(2) addresses public open spaces reserved for ventilation; Section 38 permits dealing with property consistently with the sanctioned scheme; and Section 38A prohibits disposal of park and playground areas for other purposes. The Court treated the later amendments to Sections 16 and 38A as clarifying the legislative intent to preserve public open space. It relied on Kharak Singh v. State of U.P., Municipal Council, Ratlam v. Vardhichand, Francis Coralie Mullin v. Administrator, Union Territory of Delhi, Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation, State of Himachal Pradesh v. Umed Ram Sharma, and Vikram Deo Singh Tomar v. State of Bihar on public welfare and quality of life, and on T. Damodhar Rao v. Special Officer, Municipal Corporation of Hyderabad concerning environmental protection.

predicates.writ_challenge_to_public_space_diversion: A person or group brought a writ challenge to the diversion of land reserved for public open space.
predicates.land_reserved_for_public_park: A duly sanctioned scheme reserved the land for a public park or playground.
predicates.land_allotted_for_a_different_private_us: The land was allotted to a private party for a use other than the reserved public-space purpose.

issues.definition: When a writ challenge concerns land reserved for a public park that has been allotted to a private party for another use, the diversion and allotment are invalid.

issues.legal_issue: Residents with a sufficient interest in protecting their locality’s environment and public facilities may challenge unlawful administrative action by writ petition without proving individual personal injury.
material_facts: The challengers were residents of the locality affected by the conversion of its reserved park into a site for a private hospital.
They sought to protect the public open space, local environment, and facilities intended for the enjoyment and health of the public.
The challenge raised whether the authorities had acted contrary to the law and the sanctioned scheme.
issues.conclusion: The residents had locus standi to bring the writ petition.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the broadened public-interest standing principle that sufficient interest, rather than narrowly defined personal injury, may support a writ challenge to public administrative action. Residents seeking protection of their locality’s environment and public facilities are not mere interlopers. The Court relied on S.P. Gupta v. Union of India, Akhil Bhartiya Soshit Karamchari Sangh v. Union of India, and Fertilizer Corporation Kamgar Union v. Union of India.

predicates.writ_challenge_to_public_administrative_: A writ petition was brought to challenge administrative action affecting a public interest.
predicates.challengers_are_local_residents: The challengers live in the locality affected by the administrative action.
predicates.action_threatens_local_public_environmen: The challenged action threatens the locality’s environment or public facilities.

issues.definition: When local residents bring a writ challenge to administrative action threatening their locality’s environment or public facilities, they have standing to bring it.
